CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. The kayamba is a shaker used mainly at the (1 mark)
   A. Kenyan highlands only
   B. Kenyan coast
   C. North of Lake Victoria only
   D. Northern desert only

2. To identify an instrument we give its name, its community and (1 mark)
   A. the colour of the shop
   B. how it is played
   C. its price
   D. the name of the shop

3. A thumb piano produces sound when you (1 mark)
   A. pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   B. blow into it
   C. rub its skin
   D. hit it with a big stick

4. What is the first step in improvising an accompaniment to a song? (1 mark)
   A. Stop singing
   B. Change the words
   C. Buy a drum
   D. Find the steady beat

5. Which is a rule break in netball? (1 mark)
   A. Pushing another player
   B. Catching with two hands
   C. Pivoting on one foot
   D. Passing to a teammate

6. How long may a player hold the ball before passing or shooting? (1 mark)
   A. Three seconds
   B. Ten seconds
   C. As long as they like
   D. One minute

7. Who stops the game with a whistle for a rule break? (1 mark)
   A. The goal keeper
   B. The shooter
   C. The spectator
   D. The umpire

8. How should a good netball player treat the other team at the end? (1 mark)
   A. Shout at them
   B. Tease them
   C. Shake hands and thank them
   D. Ignore them

9. Yellow mixed with blue makes (1 mark)
   A. purple
   B. orange
   C. pink
   D. green

10. Which colour is a secondary colour? (1 mark)
   A. Red
   B. Green
   C. Blue
   D. Yellow

11. How many boxes are on the scale strip in this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Ten
   C. Five
   D. One

12. On the colour wheel, green sits between (1 mark)
   A. yellow and blue
   B. red and blue
   C. orange and purple
   D. red and yellow

13. Which pattern has three beats of sound and one beat of silence? (1 mark)
   A. taa taa taa taa
   B. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   C. (rest) (rest) (rest) (rest)
   D. taa taa taa (rest)

14. A pair of quavers together lasts (1 mark)
   A. two beats
   B. one beat
   C. half a beat
   D. four beats

15. Which is a quality of a good rhythmic pattern? (1 mark)
   A. Only one kind of note
   B. Variation of note values
   C. No beat
   D. Ending on a rest always

16. Which of these letters has neither an ascender nor a descender? (1 mark)
   A. a
   B. p
   C. b
   D. d

17. The sol-fa syllable r is pronounced (1 mark)
   A. ray
   B. roh
   C. ree
   D. rah

18. A coil of clay is (1 mark)
   A. a hard brick
   B. a plate
   C. a flat sheet
   D. a long thin roll like a snake

19. How can you make a slab of even thickness? (1 mark)
   A. Drop it on the floor
   B. Squeeze with one hand
   C. Freeze it
   D. Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness

20. In the worked melody of this lesson, the last note is (1 mark)
   A. m, a quaver
   B. r, a rest
   C. a pair of quavers
   D. d, a crotchet

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write a melody that goes up by steps from d to m and comes down to d, and state the number of notes. (3 marks)

22. Explain how to tie an overhand knot. (3 marks)

23. Describe a full netball court. (3 marks)

24. Describe how to paint a fruit so that it looks round using colour value. (4 marks)

25. Describe the Kodaly hand sign for each of d, r and m. (3 marks)

26. Explain what tone or value means in a drawing. (3 marks)

27. Describe the steps of modelling the letters d, r and m on clay slabs. (5 marks)

28. State three qualities of a good melody. (3 marks)

29. Explain how you decide whether a percussion instrument is melodic or non-melodic. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — Kenyan coast
   The kayamba is a coastal shaker used by the Mijikenda and other coastal people.

2. B — how it is played
   Identifying uses name, community and method of playing.

3. A — pluck its metal tongues with your thumbs
   The kalimba or mbira has metal tongues that you pluck with the thumbs.

4. D — Find the steady beat
   You must find the beat before you can add patterns.

5. A — Pushing another player
   Contact such as pushing is not allowed.

6. A — Three seconds
   A player must pass or shoot within three seconds.

7. D — The umpire
   Umpires control the game and blow the whistle.

8. C — Shake hands and thank them
   Fair play means being respectful whether you win or lose.

9. D — green
   Yellow and blue give green.

10. B — Green
   Green is made from yellow and blue.

11. C — Five
   The strip is divided into five equal boxes.

12. A — yellow and blue
   Green sits between the two primary colours that make it.

13. D — taa taa taa (rest)
   Only the first has a single rest and three sounding beats.

14. B — one beat
   Two half beats make one whole beat.

15. B — Variation of note values
   Good patterns vary the note values.

16. A — a
   The letter a sits between the baseline and the top of small letters.

17. A — ray
   The syllable r is ray.

18. D — a long thin roll like a snake
   A coil is a long, thin, even roll of clay.

19. D — Roll the clay with a bottle between two sticks of equal thickness
   Equal sticks on both sides keep the slab even.

20. D — d, a crotchet
   The final note is d, on a crotchet.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: d r m r d. There are five notes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for going up, 1 mark for coming down, 1 mark for five.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: Make a loop with the cord. Pass the end through the loop. Pull both ends to tighten.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is a rectangle 30.5 metres long and 15.25 metres wide. It is divided into three equal thirds. It has a goal post at each end with a goal circle and a centre circle in the middle.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the rectangle with measurements, 1 mark for thirds, 1 mark for circles or posts.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Draw the outline. Paint the main colour. Add a lighter tone on the side facing the light and a darker tone on the side away from the light. Blend the edges and add a shadow.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: d is a closed fist, r is a sloping palm, m is a flat palm held level.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Tone means how light or dark an area is. In a charcoal drawing, we can make tones from light grey to black by pressing lightly or hard.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for lightness or darkness, 1 mark for range of tones, 1 mark for charcoal pressure.

27. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare and knead clay. Roll a slab and cut three rectangles of different sizes. Make coils. Shape a coil into each letter and scratch and wet where they join. Press on gently, smooth, and let dry slowly in the shade.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for preparing clay, cutting slabs, making coils, joining, and drying.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Stepwise motion, variation of syllables and note lengths, and ending on d.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Listen to the sounds. If it plays different notes, high and low, that make a tune, it is melodic. If it gives only a beat or one kind of sound, it is non-melodic.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for listening, 1 mark for melodic meaning, 1 mark for non-melodic meaning.
